what: Ryman Hospitality owns the Gaylord hotels: enormous resorts built around convention space in Nashville, Orlando, Dallas, Washington and Denver. It also owns the Grand Ole Opry and Nashville entertainment venues.
customers: Large groups and associations booking conventions years ahead, plus leisure travellers and country music audiences.
money: the Grand Ole Opry, Ryman Auditorium and Nashville venues
moat: Convention resorts of this size cannot be built again economically, and groups book two to four years ahead, which makes revenue unusually visible for a hotel owner.
risks: Group travel budgets are cut quickly in a recession
32 times earnings for a hotel owner, a full valuation
opportunities: Revenue grew from $939M to $2.6B in four years as group travel recovered
Group bookings on the books for future years are at record levels
The Nashville entertainment business grows independently of the hotels and earns high margins
watch: Group revenue on the books for the next two years, and revenue per available room.
